isf.label: Insulin sensitivity (ISF)
isf.notes: Your stated 1.5 mmol/L per unit (27). The Oct 10 refit across all logs agrees (27 fits best; 30 was slightly too strong).

crAM.label: Carb ratio, morning (05–11)
crAM.notes: Oct 9 breakfast was underdosed at 1:9; Oct 10 breakfast at ≈1:7 landed on target.

crDay.label: Carb ratio, rest of day
crDay.notes: Refit on Oct 9–10 lunches and dinners: 1:10 fits best. Sweets alone (Oct 9 cake) behaved stronger, about 1:7.

csf.label: Fast-sugar rise
csf.notes: From 16 g of regular cola on Oct 9, 00:39. Used for juice, sugar water and cola.

kMeal.label: Meal absorption
kMeal.notes: Ordinary meals and the fast part of fatty meals.

kFruit.label: Fruit absorption
kFruit.notes: Fresh and dried fruit (figs, cherries, mango). Faster than meals: the Oct 12 figs and cherries rose within 30 min, which the 35-min meal curve flattened.

giPow.label: Glycemic index: speed effect
giPow.notes: Each food's GI scales its absorption speed relative to a reference (GI 55 for food, 65 for drinks): absorption time × (ref ÷ GI)^this. 0 turns GI off.

giMag.label: Glycemic index: size effect
giMag.notes: Optionally scales how much a food raises glucose: carbs × (GI ÷ ref)^this. At 1 this is the same as dosing by glycemic load (GL = carbs × GI ÷ 100) instead of carbs. Tested Oct 12: it made forecasts worse (MAE 17.5 → 18.8), so it is off; GL is shown on each food for reference.

oneU.label: Single-unit dose delivery
oneU.notes: Vlad notes that a single 1 U press on his pens may not be fully delivered (low plunger pressure). This scales any 1 U dose; 1 = full.

kSlow.label: Fatty-meal absorption
kSlow.notes: Pizza, khachapuri, khinkali, tolma, ice cream, pastry, bread with cheese. Fat and protein slow carbs to a 2–4 h curve.

fatSlow.label: Fatty meal: slow share
fatSlow.notes: About 30% of a fatty meal's carbs arrive on the slow curve (peak ≈90 min, tail 3–4 h); the rest behave like a normal meal.

walkBoost.label: Walking: insulin boost
walkBoost.notes: Fitted at 1.0: once fatty-meal timing is modelled, the Oct 10 walk shows no extra insulin effect the data can separate. Studies usually show 1.2–1.5× during moderate walking; set it per walk once a walk without a fatty meal is logged.

walkDrop.label: Walking: direct glucose use
walkDrop.notes: Working muscles take up glucose without insulin. Lowers the forecast by this much per hour while walking, fading over the after-effect time below. Fitted Oct 12: 20/h lifts today's hits 35→38 of 43 (MAE 17.0→14.2); 40+/h made forecasts worse.

walkDropTail.label: Walking: direct-use after-effect
walkDropTail.notes: How long the direct glucose use keeps going after a walk ends, fading linearly. Tested 1, 2 and 4 h: anything over ~1 h made past forecasts worse (all-data hits 75% → 61% at 4 h), including after the 5 h walk on Oct 10 and the Oct 11 walk that was followed by a 3 h plateau near 200. Will be refitted if tonight shows a slow overnight fall after the 2 h walk.

walkTail.label: Walking: after-effect
walkTail.notes: The boost fades linearly over this many hours after the walk ends.

alcDrop.label: Alcohol: liver block
alcDrop.notes: Alcohol blocks the liver's glucose release, spread over 2–10 h after the drink. The Oct 10 lager: the drift after 23:00 fits about 40 mg/dL per drink. One evening only; the overnight readings will confirm it.

drift.label: Background drift
drift.notes: Tresiba off-schedule Oct 8–12. Set once a clean fasting stretch is logged.
